audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL block processing, transaction execution, state trie operations, EVM bytecode deployment, contract deployment validation, GraphQL/JSON-RPC APIs, difficulty calculation, Clique PoA consensus, the PoW-to-PoS merge transition, and in-protocol builder mechanisms. Both EL and CL interfaces are materially present.

in_scope: Engine API interface (fork choice updates, payload proposals)

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM SLOAD/SSTORE operations are internal EL components, not external entities. The EVM is part of the execution layer under audit.
In EIP-1459 context, the 'Ethereum Client' performing DNS discovery is the system under audit itself, not an external entity. The DNS resolver is the true external entity.
Client configuration providing enrtree URLs is internal to the node setup, not an external entity sending data across a trust boundary at runtime.
In EIP-2256 context, the user wallet is part of the system under audit (it processes the RPC request). The dApp is the external entity.
In Gloas builder context, the builder's local execution engine is an internal component, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.
In EIP-225 Clique context, the local signer is the node itself producing blocks. It is an internal component, not an external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P devp2p protocol (NewBlock, NewBlockHashes, block/tx gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the P2P network and send arbitrary blocks, transactions, or messages. Covers EXT-NETWORK-PEER, EXT-PEER-NODE from Frontier, EIP-3675, EIP-4345, EIP-225.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and dApps submit transactions and queries via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All input is potentially malicious. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-DAPP, EXT-USER, EXT-DEPLOYER.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via GraphQL API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: GraphQL API on port 8547 (/graphql endpoint, sendRawTransaction mutation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: GraphQL API is unauthenticated by default per EIP-1767. No built-in rate limiting or access control. Covers EXT-CLIENT, EXT-TRANSACTION-SUBMITTER, EXT-API-CLIENT from EIP-1767.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Resolver via DNS Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: DNS TXT record resolution (EIP-1459 enrtree protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DNS infrastructure is untrusted. Responses may be spoofed, corrupted, or served by compromised resolvers. Signature verification provides integrity but DNS itself is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL communicates via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Channel is authenticated but payload content (execution payloads, fork choice state, head/safe/finalized hashes) must still be validated. Covers EXT-BEACON-CHAIN from EIP-3675.

trusted_external_entities.name: PoW Miner via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners are untrusted network participants. Blocks may have manipulated difficulty, invalid headers, or attempt to trigger premature TTD. Covers EXT-MINER from EIP-3675, EIP-4345.

trusted_external_entities.name: Authorized Clique Signer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation with ECDSA-signed headers (EIP-225 Clique)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Even authorized Clique signers are untrusted for block content. Signing authorization is verified but block content, votes, and timestamps require full validation. Covers EXT-AUTHORIZED-SIGNER from EIP-225.

trusted_external_entities.name: Message Signer via Transaction/Contract Call
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract function calls with signed messages (CHAINID-based replay protection)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External users submitting signed messages for contract verification are untrusted. Signatures may originate from different chains (replay attempt). Covers EXT-USER from EIP-1344.

trusted_external_entities.name: Builder via Gossip Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: execution_payload_bid gossip topic, execution_payload gossip topic
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builders submit bids and envelopes via P2P gossip. BLS signatures authenticate builder identity but bid content (value, payload, state_root) requires full validation. Covers EXT-PROPOSER interaction and EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT from Gloas.

trusted_external_entities.name: Builder Deposit via EL Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builder registration occurs via untrusted EL transactions. Withdrawal credentials format and deposit amounts must be validated. Covers EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT from Gloas.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: header fields, transaction validity, state root verification, gas limit checks. All block data is untrusted.
Full transaction validation required: ECDSA signature recovery, nonce check, balance check, gas limit validation, RLP decoding. All transaction data is untrusted.
Full transaction validation plus 0xEF first-byte check on returned runtime bytecode. Init code execution must be gas-bounded. Exceptional abort on reserved 0xEF prefix.

Query parsing and schema validation required. Operation type must be checked (signing, compiling, mining operations denied). Input scalar types (Bytes32, Address, BigInt) must be format-validated. No built-in auth - external access control assumed.
RLP-encoded transaction must be decoded and fully validated before broadcast. Same validation as JSON-RPC transaction submission.

Root record signature must be verified against known secp256k1 public key. Sequence number must be >= cached value (anti-rollback). Branch content must match subdomain hash (keccak256). Multiple independent DNS sources should be used to mitigate eclipse attacks.

JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payload content must be fully validated: deprecated PoW fields (difficulty=0, nonce=0, ommers empty, mixHash=0), state root, transaction execution. Fork choice state (head, safe, finalized hashes) must reference known valid blocks.

Full PoW validation: difficulty target verification, total difficulty computation against TTD, ethash proof verification. Blocks claiming to reach TTD must be carefully validated to prevent premature or malicious merge triggering.

ECDSA signature must be recovered and signer verified against authorized set. Signing frequency limit enforced (1 per floor(N/2)+1 blocks). Timestamp >= parent + BLOCK_PERIOD. ExtraData format validated. Checkpoint blocks require embedded signer list, nonce=0, beneficiary=0. Vote tallying for signer set changes requires majority threshold.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Smart contract call with signed message (CHAINID verification)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Contract must extract chain ID from signed message and compare against CHAINID opcode result. Mismatch indicates cross-chain replay attempt and must be rejected.

Builder BLS signature must be verified against registered builder_index. Builder must have sufficient excess balance for bid value. execution_payment must equal zero for gossip bids. parent_block_hash and parent_block_root must reference valid chain state. Slot must be current or next.

Envelope must match previously accepted bid (block_hash). Builder signature must be verified. State root must be correct (computed from process_execution_payload). Payload content must pass full EL validation.
Withdrawal credentials must have BUILDER_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x03). Address format must be validated. Deposit amount must meet minimum requirements.

Address parameter must be valid Ethereum format. ChainId, limit, and asset types must be validated. User consent must be obtained before returning asset data. Only whitelisted assets should be shared. dApp identity should be verified to prevent phishing.
